results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

...

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds

...

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |

| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |

| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |

...

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

results.title: GPU Rental Price Report, November 2026 · EverXCloud
highlights:
Public GPU-hour prices for H100, H200, B200, A100, L40S, RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 across 16 cloud providers, with medians and spreads.

## Executive summary

EverXCloud read the public pricing pages of 16 GPU cloud providers on 2026-10-26 and recorded 75 prices per GPU-hour for eight GPUs. On-demand prices for the same GPU still vary widely between providers, and spot, preemptible or community capacity costs far less than on-demand capacity.

This report covers third-party list prices only. Once the EverXCloud Marketplace launches, its own price index will be published from real transactions.

## Key findings

1. The median on-demand H100 SXM price across 11 providers is $3.99 per GPU-hour, from $3.14 to $6.16: the most expensive listing costs 2.0× the cheapest.
2. Spot, preemptible and community H100 SXM capacity has a median of $2.30 per GPU-hour across 3 providers, 42% below the on-demand median.
3. The H200 carries a 24% premium over the H100 SXM at the median ($4.94 vs $3.99 on demand, 10 providers).
4. On-demand B200 prices range from $6.00 to $8.60 per GPU-hour across 7 providers, with a median of $8.19.
5. The A100 80GB shows the widest relative spread among data center GPUs: 2.6× between the cheapest ($1.09) and the most expensive ($2.79) on-demand listing, across 9 providers.
6. AWS Capacity Blocks, a short-term reservation, list the H100 at $5.97 and the B200 at $14.21 per GPU-hour, 1.5× and 1.7× the on-demand medians of the other providers.

## Prices by GPU

Spot, preemptible or community, USD per GPU-hour

| GPU | Min | Median | Max | Max ÷ min | Providers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $1.99 | $2.30 | $2.69 | 1.4× | 3 |
| H100 PCIe | $1.99 | $1.99 | $1.99 | 1.0× | 1 |
| H200 | $2.99 | $3.00 | $3.59 | 1.2× | 3 |
| B200 | $4.09 | $4.26 | $5.98 | 1.5× | 3 |
| A100 80GB | $1.08 | $1.08 | $1.19 | 1.1× | 3 |
| L40S | $0.79 | $0.85 | $0.91 | 1.2× | 2 |
| RTX 4090 | $0.16 | $0.34 | $0.65 | 4.1× | 3 |
| RTX 5090 | $0.25 | $0.47 | $0.69 | 2.8× | 2 |

...

- Prices were read on 2026-10-26 on each provider's official public pricing page, in USD per GPU-hour, excluding tax. No price was estimated, negotiated or taken from a third-party aggregator.
- One price per provider, GPU and offer type. When a provider lists several configurations for the same GPU, the lowest listed price was kept, and the listing is recorded in the data.
- Multi-GPU instances are converted to a per-GPU price by dividing the instance price by the number of GPUs (for example CoreWeave and AWS 8-GPU instances).
- On-demand and spot, preemptible or community prices are reported separately. AWS prices are Capacity Block rates, a short-term reservation, and are not included in the on-demand statistics.
- Providers whose pricing page could not be read, showed prices only after sign-in or on request, or did not map prices to GPUs unambiguously were left out: Vast.ai, Crusoe, Vultr, TensorDock, Fluidstack, Genesis Cloud, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Voltage Park, Cudo Compute, Scaleway, Paperspace and SF Compute.
- The median of an even number of prices is the mean of the two middle values.

results.title: The Cheapest GPU Rental Right Now (November 2026): What 'Cheapest' Actually Means for H100, H200, and B200
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
The takeaway

- Entering November 2026, the cheapest GPU rental depends entirely on which 'cheapest' you mean: the marketplace/spot floor, a reliable named on-demand rate, or the market median — and they can differ by 2–4x on the same card.
- Cheapest reliable on-demand right now: H100 (80GB) ~$1.99–2.89/GPU-hr (Voltage Park ~$1.99, Thunder Compute ~$2.19, RunPod ~$2.89), H200 (141GB) ~$3.59–4.29 (RunPod ~$3.59, Crusoe ~$4.29), B200 (Blackwell) ~$5.50–6.99 (Lambda is the cheapest reliable on-demand B200).
- Marketplace/spot floors go lower and less certain: H100 asks from ~$1.74 (Vast.ai) and spot ~$1.03 (Spheron), H200 asks from ~$2.25–2.76, B200 single-provider floors as low as ~$3.69 but with availability and trust caveats.
- Market medians are much higher: ~$4.20 H100, ~$5.70 H200, ~$8.19 B200 (Uvik's October index) — so a random provider costs roughly double the floor.
- Hyperscalers (AWS/Azure/GCP) stay ~$7–14/hr for the identical card — you pay 3–6x for the platform, not the silicon.
- The real cheapest option is often NOT renting: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API beats renting metal at any of these rates, because a rented GPU bills 24/7 whether it works or not.
- And the direction of travel just changed: with Microsoft and Google pausing capex and chip delays pushing capacity to H1 2027, the price floor that stopped falling in October is now firming — the cheapest rate you see today may be the cheapest you'll see for a while.

...

**The cheapest reliable on-demand rate right now (November 2026):**

- H100 (80GB) → ~$1.99–2.89/GPU-hr. Voltage Park ~$1.99, Thunder Compute ~$2.19, RunPod ~$2.89.
- H200 (141GB) → ~$3.59–4.29/hr. RunPod ~$3.59, Crusoe ~$4.29.
- B200 (Blackwell) → ~$5.50–6.99/hr. Lambda is typically the cheapest reliable on-demand Blackwell.

...

Every figure here is a published rate gathered at the end of October 2026 from public pricing pages and multi-provider trackers (getdeploying, Ornn, Uvik, Singularity, Spheron). They move weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read them for the shape, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.
